explain.say: In 1488 the Portuguese captain Bartolomeu Dias rounded the southern tip of Africa, later named the Cape of Good Hope. Within thirty-four years, ships from Portugal and Spain had reached India, the Americas and sailed around the globe. Look at the timeline. Why did two small kingdoms on Europe's edge lead the way?

explain.say: See the causes. They wanted spices and gold without Italian and Muslim middlemen, their kings competed fiercely, and they had caravels, light ships that could sail into the wind, plus knowledge of Atlantic wind patterns. Crusading zeal and mission mattered too. Which cause do you think came first?

explain.say: Follow the map. Vasco da Gama sailed from Lisbon round the Cape and, guided by a local pilot from Malindi in East Africa, reached Calicut in India in 1498. Columbus, sailing for Spain, landed in the Bahamas in 1492, believing he had reached Asia. Why do you think he never admitted his mistake?

items2: Lisbon > Cape of Good Hope > India
draw.label: Da Gama and Columbus

explain.say: Were these the biggest voyages? See the sizes. Around 1405 the Chinese admiral Zheng He sailed with about 27,800 men and over two hundred ships. Da Gama had about 170 men, Columbus about 90. Size was not the point: the Iberians kept coming back, with guns and forts. What does that tell you?

In 1519 Magellan set out with five ships and about 270 men; he was killed in the Philippines, and Juan Sebastián Elcano brought 18 survivors home in 1522. For the Taíno and other peoples these voyages began conquest and catastrophe. Great work. Exam tip: show each voyage from both shores.

faq.q: Why did Portugal and Spain explore?
faq.a: To reach the spice and gold trades directly, to win glory and revenue for their crowns, to fight Muslim powers and spread Christianity, and because new ships and navigation skills made long ocean voyages possible.
asks: What were the motives for the voyages of discovery?
Did the Ottomans block the spice trade?

faq.q: What was the role of the Ottomans in the voyages?
faq.a: The old story that the Ottomans blocked the spice routes is largely a myth: Venetian and Mamluk trade continued. The Iberians wanted to bypass middlemen and their profits, not escape a closed road.
asks: Did the fall of Constantinople cause exploration?

faq.q: What was the Treaty of Tordesillas?
faq.a: A 1494 agreement between Spain and Portugal dividing newly found lands outside Europe along a line west of the Cape Verde islands: lands west to Spain, east to Portugal. It is why Brazil speaks Portuguese.
A Portuguese captain who sailed from Lisbon around Africa and, with a pilot hired in Malindi, reached Calicut in India in May 1498, opening a sea route from Europe to Asia.
asks: When did Europeans reach India by sea?

faq.a: Columbus landed in the Bahamas on 12 October 1492, meeting the Taíno. Spanish colonisation of the Caribbean followed, with forced labour, violence and disease that devastated the Taíno within a few decades.

facts: Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope in 1488.
Vasco da Gama reached Calicut in May 1498.
The Victoria returned to Spain in 1522 with 18 of the expedition's original crew.

quiz.say: Zheng He's fleet had about 27,800 men and da Gama's about 170. Roughly how many times larger was Zheng He's crew?
quiz.why: 27,800 divided by 170 is about 164, so roughly 160 times larger.

wrong.1: That would mean only about 2,700 men.
wrong.2: That would mean over a quarter of a million men.

quiz.why: The 1494 line put the eastern bulge of South America in Portugal's zone; Cabral reached it in 1500.

wrong.1: Columbus sailed for Spain and reached the Caribbean.
wrong.2: The Ottomans played no part in dividing the Americas.
